title: Icepack: run the canonical synthetic shelf
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: Your goal: run the native Icepack shelf
instructions: Launch the supplied synthetic shelf, inspect thickness and velocity, then save the result ZIP.
Start with your approved cloud account connected and resources prepared.
Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
steps.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package. Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
steps.expected: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
steps.note: Basic needs no script import or dataset upload for this supplied example. Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.

steps.title: 1. Choose the Basic example
instructions: Choose Cloud → Basic → Icepack → Tutorial / 02 Synthetic Ice Shelf.
Keep the supplied example and its default scientific configuration.
steps.why: Basic retains the supplied example; optional edits change its scientific input definition.
steps.expected: The supplied notebook is converted to run.py for cloud execution.
steps.note: The notebook is converted to run.py for cloud execution.

steps.title: 2. Retain the native time stepping
instructions: Keep 255.15 K and 200 steps in each of two 400-year phases: 2 years per step.
The second phase includes damage physics.
steps.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
steps.expected: 255.15 K; two 400-year phases; 200 steps each; dt = 2 years.
steps.note: The curved shelf has a 200 km inflow-arc radius and nominal 5 km mesh spacing.

steps.title: 3. Confirm cloud readiness
instructions: Check Account connected and Storage, Containers and Compute Ready.
Use Prepare cloud first if your resources are not ready.
steps.why: Ready indicates that the required account resources are configured for the run.
steps.expected: Use Prepare cloud first if resources are not ready.
steps.note: This run uses 2 vCPU, 8 GiB and a 60-minute time limit.

steps.title: 4. Review before submitting
instructions: Choose Review & Launch.
Confirm ICEPACK, 02-synthetic-ice-shelf and the tested image/digest.
Keep the canonical source and run.py target.
Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
This confirmation starts the run.
The execution summary names ICEPACK and 02-synthetic-ice-shelf.
Allow the job to complete, then open its results.
steps.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission. The tested image and pinned digest identify the native software environment. This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job. Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
steps.expected: Allow the job to finish, then open its results.
steps.note: Check the connected account and estimated charges before confirming. The displayed runtime is an estimate, not a measured model duration. Control guide; the following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run. The materialized run.py matches the canonical notebook exactly.

steps.title: 5. Allow time for the model
instructions: The native job succeeded with exit code 0.
Submission → container start: 223.044 s. Batch task: 427.137 s.
steps.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
steps.expected: Submission → start: 223.044 s; Batch task: 427.137 s.
steps.note: Long queue, compute and operator waits are shortened.

steps.title: 6. Choose a field to inspect
instructions: In Results choose solution icepack and select thickness or velocity.
The selected velocity field is previewed in Results.
Use Render when needed after choosing a field.
steps.why: Keep the source, versions, hashes and scientific qualifications with the result. The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
steps.expected: The exported mesh has 3,371 vertices and 6,533 triangles.
steps.note: Read the displayed field name and units. The exported mesh has 3,371 vertices and 6,533 triangles.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the saved thickness map
instructions: Open the full saved thickness PNG.
Colour is thickness in metres; x and y are metres. Final thickness spans 98.1004–350.1418 m.
steps.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
steps.expected: Final thickness: 98.1004–350.1418 m; x and y are metres.
steps.note: The full original scientific PNG is shown here.

steps.title: 8. Inspect speed and direction
instructions: Colour is speed in m/year; arrows show direction. Speed spans 160.457–740.819 m/year.
Native thickness/velocity use CG2; the portable export uses CG1.
steps.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
steps.expected: Speed: 160.457–740.819 m/year; native CG2 fields exported as CG1.
steps.note: Keep the unchanged saved PNGs with your archive.

steps.title: 9. Generate the archive link
instructions: Choose Download results below the plot.
When the link appears, open it to save the ZIP.
The result package includes fields, mesh, figures, native mesh file and provenance.
Save the 20-member ZIP and retain it with the canonical source.
steps.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together. Keep the source, versions, hashes and scientific qualifications with the result.
steps.expected: The browser-downloaded archive passed its CRC check.
steps.note: Wait for the fresh link for this run. Use the generated link for the selected run. The browser-downloaded archive passed its CRC check.

steps.title: Keep the numerical and runtime context
instructions: Runtime records Icepack 1.1.0, Firedrake 2025.10.2 and Python 3.12.13; observed MPI world size is 1.
Damage spans −0.0036016 to 0.0741413, including the retained numerical undershoot.
steps.why: Keep the scientific input definitions and numerical qualifications with the result.
steps.expected: Native damage undershoot is retained; portable fields are not a full checkpoint.
steps.note: Finite output checks passed. This portable export is not a full checkpoint or an independent repeat-equality result.
